items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Leonard Feather ... knew my reputation. I had worked with – done some things for him – knew my reputation, went all the way back with me from Chicago. So he knew me.

ctx.x: Yeah. Hold it a second, because I’m trying to remember again. I was doing a gig. None of it was thought of how important it was or how important those people were going to be and how

I would fit, because none of them were that important, that big or anything, as far as I was concerned. I was, here again, doing a gig. But once I got in the Shearing picture, then there was a need for me to do other things, other than play bass, because then George depended – I just out of the clear sky started offering suggestions. When it came time to make certain moves, I would say, George, if you’re going to do this, this is what you have to do and this is what has to happen. He began to realize, hey, this…
